players.product: complete custom XPU accelerator (packaged ASIC + HBM) delivered to hyperscalers

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 total revenue reached a record $19.3 billion, up 29% year-on-year and above guidance on better-than-expected AI semiconductor growth; semiconductor revenue was a record $12.5 billion, up 52% year-on-year; AI semiconductor revenue grew 106% year-on-year to $8.4 billion, 'way above our outlook'; adjusted EBITDA was a record $13.1 billion, 68% of revenue
quarterly_data.figure: $19.3 billion revenue (up 29%); $12.5 billion semiconductor (52%); $8.4 billion AI semiconductor (106%); $13.1 billion adjusted EBITDA

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 guidance: consolidated revenue of approximately $22 billion, up 47% year-on-year; semiconductor revenue approximately $14.8 billion, up 76%; AI semiconductor revenue $10.7 billion, up approximately 140% year-on-year; Infrastructure Software approximately $7.2 billion, up 9%; consolidated gross margin flat sequentially at 77%; adjusted EBITDA approximately 68% of revenue
quarterly_data.figure: $22 billion revenue (47%); $14.8 billion semiconductor (76%); $10.7 billion AI semiconductor (140%); 77% gross margin

quarterly_data.signal: Custom accelerator business grew 140% year-on-year in Q1, with the momentum continuing in Q2; the ramp of custom AI accelerators across all 5 customers is 'progressing very well', and Broadcom now has a sixth customer (OpenAI). Customers 4 and 5 (unnamed) see strong shipments this year, expected to more than double in 2027
quarterly_data.figure: 140% custom accelerator growth; customers 4 and 5 shipments to more than double in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Hock Tan: 'we have line of sight to achieve AI revenue from chips, just chips, in excess of $100 billion in 2027' (XPUs, switch chips and DSPs — silicon content), with the supply chain required already secured; by gigawatt, 2027 shipments are 'getting close to 10 gigawatts'. Asked about an analyst's ~$20 billion per gigawatt content estimate, Tan said chip dollars per gigawatt vary by customer, 'sometimes quite dramatically', but are 'not far from the dollars you're talking about'
quarterly_data.figure: in excess of $100 billion AI chip revenue in 2027; close to 10 gigawatts

quarterly_data.signal: Broadcom has 'fully secured capacity' of constrained components — leading-edge wafers, high-bandwidth memory and substrates — for '26 through '28; Tan said Broadcom was 'early in being able to lock up T-glass' and has 'locked up substrates'. Charlie Kawwas: customers share 2 to 3 (sometimes 4) year forecasts, securing supply required investments with partners in capacity and technology, and Broadcom can grow in '28 with the supply it sees

Inventory ended Q1 at $3 billion as Broadcom continues to secure components to support strong AI demand; days of inventory on hand rose to 68 days from 58 days in Q4 in anticipation of accelerating AI semiconductor growth; capex was $250 million
quarterly_data.figure: inventory of $3 billion; 68 days vs 58 days; $250 million capex

quarterly_data.signal: XPU design trend: most customers begin with inference (less compute), but XPUs are now used for both training and inference; the more mature customers will 'develop 2 chips each year simultaneously, one for training, one for inference', and a majority of the 6 customers are headed that way. Tan said XPU designs are becoming customized to each customer's workloads (e.g. mixture of experts) and departing from standard GPU design

Responding to an analyst's suggestion that rack shipments would dilute gross margin, Tan said gross margin will not be affected as more AI products ship ('We have gotten our yields') and the AI model will be fairly consistent with the rest of the semiconductor business; CFO Kirsten Spears said the mix impact is 'actually not going to be substantial at all'. Tan declined to split the Anthropic project between racks and chips

Non-AI semiconductor revenue of $4.1 billion was flat year-on-year (Q2 forecast approximately $4.1 billion, up 4%); Infrastructure Software revenue was $6.8 billion, up 1%; VMware revenue grew 13% year-on-year; total contract value booked in Q1 exceeded $9.2 billion, sustaining ARR growth of 19%
quarterly_data.figure: $4.1 billion non-AI semis; $6.8 billion software; VMware 13%; TCV over $9.2 billion; ARR 19%

contracts.signal: Hock Tan: 'For Anthropic, we are off to a very good start in 2026 for 1 gigawatt of TPU compute. And for '27, this demand is expected to surge in excess of 3 gigawatts of compute.' Tan declined to say how much of the project is racks versus chips
contracts.units: 1 gigawatt of TPU compute (2026); in excess of 3 gigawatts of compute (2027)

contracts.signal: Hock Tan: 'contrary to recent analyst reports, Meta's custom accelerator MTIA road map is alive and well. We're shipping now'; for the next-generation XPUs Broadcom will scale to multiple gigawatts in '27 and beyond; Tan called MTIA a strategic program for Meta, 'not optionality'

connects_to.relationship: custom XPU silicon supply and deployment

contracts.signal: OpenAI is Broadcom's sixth XPU customer: 'We expect OpenAI deploying in volume their first-generation XPU in 2027 at over 1 gigawatt of compute capacity.'

players.product: Tomahawk 5/6 and Jericho3-AI Ethernet switch ASICs for AI fabric

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 AI networking revenue grew 60% year-on-year and represented 1/3 of total AI revenue; in Q2 AI networking is projected to grow to 40% of total AI revenue ('We are clearly gaining share in networking'); longer term Tan expects AI networking components to range between 33% to 40% of total AI revenue in any quarter, growing even faster than XPUs for now
quarterly_data.figure: 60% growth; 1/3 of AI revenue in Q1; 40% in Q2; 33% to 40% range

quarterly_data.signal: In scale-out, the first-to-market Tomahawk 6 switch at 100 terabit per second and Broadcom's 200G SerDes are capturing demand from hyperscalers using XPUs or GPUs; Tan said there is 'huge demand for this only 100 terabit per second switch out there'. Next-generation Tomahawk 7 with double the performance launches in '27
quarterly_data.figure: Tomahawk 6: 100 terabit per second; 200G SerDes; Tomahawk 7 2x performance in '27

quarterly_data.signal: Charlie Kawwas: Ethernet became the scale-out protocol of choice for GPU and XPU clusters, and Broadcom is consistently hearing Ethernet is the right answer for scale-up too; many of the XPU designs Broadcom is doing are being asked to scale-up through Ethernet

players.product: TPU v7 ASIC design / SerDes IP co-development

connects_to.relationship: co-designed TPU v7 silicon delivered to Google

contracts.signal: Hock Tan: 'For Google, we continue our trajectory of growth in '26 with strong demand for the seventh-generation Ironwood TPU. In 2027 and beyond, we expect to see even stronger demand from next generations of TPU.'

players.product: Tomahawk 5 switch ASIC and PAM4 DSP

quarterly_data.signal: Hock Tan: in scale-out, customers are running optical transceivers at 1.6 terabit and 'We are again the only player out there doing DSP at 1.6 terabit'; combined with Tomahawk 6 this is driving networking component growth faster than XPUs

Scale-up stays on copper: Broadcom's 200G SerDes lets XPU customers stay on direct attached copper, and as it steps up to 400G SerDes in 2028 customers will likely continue on copper, since optical is more expensive and uses significantly more power. Tan: 'you don't need to go run into some bright shiny objects called CPO, even as we are the lead in CPOs. CPOs will come in its time, not this year, maybe not next year'; scale-out already uses optical
